body:
WHAT
The version tool asks git about the repository through a small wrapper that runs execFileSync('git', args) with no shell. versionTags lists tags matching '<prefix>N.N.N*' sorted newest version first (legacy four-part tags like v0.13.0.1 are accepted and their build number breaks ties). commitsSince reads commits after a tag (or all of HEAD) oldest first with hash, short hash, subject and body split by control characters. originUrl, githubHttpsUrl and hasUncommittedChanges report the remote, its https form, and whether the tree is dirty.

WHY
Deciding a release from wrong or missing history would re-release an old version or duplicate changelog entries; a wrapper that mutated the repo or ran through a shell could rewrite history or execute text from a branch name.

WHERE
tools/version/lib/git.mjs — git(args, {cwd}), repositoryRoot(from), versionTags(root, tagPrefix), commitsSince(root, fromTag), FIELD/RECORD separators, originUrl(root), githubHttpsUrl(url), hasUncommittedChanges(root); uses parse/compare/legacyBuild from tools/version/lib/version.mjs.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. In a temp git repo (git init, one commit, tags v0.1.0, v0.2.0, v0.13.0.0, v0.13.0.1, vfoo), versionTags(root,'v') returns [v0.13.0.1, v0.13.0.0, v0.2.0, v0.1.0] in that order (build breaks the tie) and ignores 'vfoo'; a repo with no tags returns [].
2. commitsSince(root, 'v0.1.0') returns only commits after that tag, oldest first, excluding merge commits, with subject and body correctly split even when a body contains newlines; commitsSince(root, null) on an empty repository (no commits) returns [] instead of throwing.
3. githubHttpsUrl maps 'git@github.com:owner/name.git', 'https://github.com/owner/name.git' and 'https://github.com/owner/name' all to 'https://github.com/owner/name', and returns null for null or a non-GitHub URL; originUrl returns null in a repo with no origin remote.
4. hasUncommittedChanges is false right after a commit, true after creating an untracked file, and false again after committing it.
5. After running every exported function against the temp repo, `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git tag --list`, `git status --porcelain` and the reflog are identical to before (snapshot and compare), proving the module is read-only; and every execFileSync call passes 'git' as the file with an argv array and no shell option.
